note:
New batch for the /collections/serums header. Malcolm: 'lets try a combination of the full fore arm in view but also with a subtle gradient.'

TWO CHANGES ON TOP OF WHAT ROUND 1 ALREADY FIXED. Round 1 corrected the product — the full seven-element label quoted verbatim and the serum described as a liquid rather than an opaque fill — and both of those carry forward unchanged here. What is new:

  * FULL FOREARM. Every banner in this library crops the arm at the wrist or mid-forearm, so the bottle appears to float beside the face with a disembodied hand. Here the arm is in view from elbow to fingertips, running up through the frame, which gives the shot a real gesture and reads as a person using a product rather than a product composited next to a person. Stated as a measured path — elbow low and inside the lower edge, forearm rising diagonally, bottle at the top of that line — because 'full forearm' on its own is the kind of description that six engines each interpret differently.
  * SUBTLE GRADIENT. The backdrop has been flat graphite on every banner so far, which is why extending the canvas has been easy and also why the shots read a little airless. A soft gradient is asked for explicitly, with the direction and the two end tones named, and with banding negated — a gradient rendered in 8-bit across 3000px is exactly where banding shows.

WHAT THE GRADIENT COSTS DOWNSTREAM, AND WHY IT IS STILL BRIEFED THIS WAY. extend-banner-canvas.py builds its extension from the shot's own edge profile, so a vertical gradient extends cleanly — the profile IS the gradient. A gradient running horizontally would not: the extension would continue the last column's tone flat and the join would show as the point where the gradient stops. So the brief asks for the light to fall vertically or diagonally-from-above, never left-to-right, and for the frame's own left edge to stay even top to bottom.

COMPOSITION. Subject and bottle to the RIGHT, clear gradient space to the LEFT for the heading, so the canvas extends leftward the way the other collection banners do.

Generated at 3072x1272 to match the source aspect the extender is tuned for. Class A with legible branding, so FLUX.2 is barred; Luma has refused this subject family all session and is left out rather than burning four minutes to fail again.

slots.title: Full forearm, gradient backdrop, subject right
slots.prompt: Editorial beauty photograph, very wide cinematic frame, of one Caucasian woman around thirty five years old, keeping the same woman, colouring and register as the first reference image. She sits in the RIGHT half of the frame, turned three quarters toward the light, looking calmly just past the camera, her whole face in view and sharp, hair swept back, bare shoulders, almost no makeup. Her ARM IS IN VIEW IN FULL: the elbow rests low and just inside the bottom edge of the frame, the forearm rises diagonally up and inward across the right of the picture, and her hand holds the bottle upright at cheek height at the top of that line, so the whole limb reads as one continuous gesture from elbow to fingertips. Nothing crops the arm. Real skin kept real on the arm as well as the face: visible pores, fine hairs catching the light along the forearm, natural fine lines, no airbrushing and no allover repeating pattern anywhere. Her fingers are relaxed around the lower third of the glass, well clear of the lettering. Behind her the backdrop is a SUBTLE GRADIENT, not a flat wall: deep near-black charcoal at the top of the frame easing smoothly down to a slightly lighter warm charcoal toward the bottom, the change gentle and continuous with no visible steps, bands or edges, and no spotlight pool. The light falls from above, so the gradient runs vertically down the frame and never left to right; the extreme LEFT edge of the frame stays even in tone from top to bottom. The LEFT THIRD of the picture is empty backdrop with no part of her, her hair, her arm or the bottle entering it, so a headline can sit there. The bottle is the product in the second reference image: a 30ml FROSTED COLOURLESS glass dropper bottle, straight-sided with softly rounded shoulders, a tall brushed silver aluminium collar and a translucent white rubber-bulb pipette. Inside it the serum is a CLEAR, COLOURLESS, WATER-TRANSPARENT liquid that reads as a liquid and not as a solid fill: the glass pipette stem is visible standing in it, a faint meniscus marks the fill line near the top, and the air space above that line is visibly empty. Reproduce the front label exactly as in the second reference, every character verbatim, in this order, with these weights: the Skingenetix DNA double-helix mark in black at the top, the wordmark 'Skingenetix' in bold black beneath it, then a thin vertical silver rule down the left of the text block, and beside that rule 'ACETYL' and 'HEXAPEPTIDE-8' in bold black capitals on two lines, 'ANTI-WRINKLE' and 'SERUM' in mid-grey capitals on two lines, 'PREMIUM FORMULA' in plain black capitals, and at the foot '10% ACETYL HEXAPEPTIDE-8 | 30ML' in small black capitals. Do not add, remove, reorder or restyle any word. The label is turned square to camera, is the plane of focus and the sharpest thing in the picture, every character crisply edged and legible down to the smallest line. 85mm at f4, fine film grain, quiet and expensive.
